candidates.exact_span: technology-based or water quality-based effluent limitations

candidates.exact_span: This permit may be reopened to establish effluent limitations for the parameter(s) to be consistent with that approved State standards in accordance with 40 CFR 122.44(d). Modification of the permit is subject to the provisions of 40 CFR 124.5.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Prospective WQS or TMDL-based reopening could be interpreted as potentially altering applicable effluent limits or adding conditions; that affects which limits and requirements are treated as currently binding versus contingent on future action.

candidates.exact_span: The limitations and monitoring requirements set forth in the proposed permit are developed from the State water quality standards and are protective of those designated uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Tying limits and monitoring to State water quality standards affects which parameters have enforceable numeric limits versus report-only obligations, and which monitoring requirements are deemed applicable under the proposed permit.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent discharges flows are intermittent and are not directly discharged to Animas River.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Intermittent discharge and indirect routing to the receiving water can change when discharge-based or receiving-water-based monitoring is required, and whether periods without discharge are documented no-discharge intervals versus unresolved missing-evidence cases.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Reported flow magnitude and the assertion that flows have not increased can affect flow-dependent limit applicability and whether absence of measurements aligns with documented low or no-discharge conditions.

candidates.computation_change_reason: Antibacksliding language governs whether a proposed limit may be less stringent than the prior permit; interpretation of the material-alterations exception changes which numeric limit is enforceable for a parameter.
